content: 1. Activities related to contact tracing that were not observed in the past 24 hours are documented under Number 3. 2. Quality assurance checks for contact tracing were conducted today, and the findings are recorded under Notes Number 4. 3. Observations made by the contact follow-up team during today's activities are detailed under Notes Number 5. 4. Alerts raised today for symptomatic contacts are documented under Notes Number 6. 5. Additional notes from today's activities are recorded under Notes iv. 6. This form is a recommended tool for use by the intended user. The data collected through this form is not intended for use in the CDC's data collection system, and the CDC does not plan to collect this information. 7. The emergency guideline for implementing and managing contact tracing for Ebola Virus Disease includes a sample equipment list for the Contact Tracing Team. This team comprises a lead epidemiologist, supervisors, investigation teams, contact follow-up teams, and a data manager. 8. Personal protective equipment (PPE) required includes disposable gloves, gowns, face shields or goggles, N95/FFP2 masks, surgical masks for cases, and biohazard plastic bags. 9. Information technology tools such as GPS devices, cell phones with credit, computers, internet access, and electronic data collection tools are essential. 10. Field equipment includes thermometers (noting that infrared thermometers may be less accurate in non-ideal conditions), office supplies (e.g., paper, pens, folders), weather-appropriate gear (e.g., raincoats, boots), hand sanitizers or bleach, and appropriate forms. 11. Transportation resources include drivers and vehicles, with considerations for fuel, rental vehicles, or taxis if needed. 12. The emergency guideline emphasizes that subjective fever or other symptoms in a contact should raise suspicion, and temperature measurements should not be overly relied upon, especially in arid or extreme environments. 13. Setting up a functional contact tracing system requires significant human, financial, and logistical resources. Budgetary considerations include salaries for key personnel (e.g., epidemiologists, supervisors, data managers, drivers) and costs for equipment, cell phone credits, printing forms, and hand sanitizers. 14. Essential staff for contact tracing include: A lead epidemiologist at the national level with outbreak response experience. Field epidemiologists in each affected district to oversee supervisors and prioritize contacts for follow-up. Data managers to ensure accurate data entry, reporting, and coordination across districts. Investigation teams comprising epidemiologists, clinicians, psychosocial experts, and health communication specialists to identify and interview contacts. Supervisors to oversee contact follow-up teams and address field challenges. Contact follow-up teams to visit contacts daily for 21 days, monitor health status, and report findings. 15. Other teams include: Transportation teams to safely transport suspected, probable, and confirmed cases to isolation units, equipped with disinfectable vehicles and trained in infection prevention. Disinfection teams to sanitize locations associated with cases and coordinate with burial and transportation teams. Burial teams to conduct safe and dignified burials for probable and confirmed cases, ensuring infection control measures are followed. 16. Recommended training modules for contact tracing include: A one-day training course for contact follow-up teams and supervisors to understand Ebola Virus Disease (EVD), its transmission, infection prevention, and contact tracing procedures. A two-day training course for epidemiologists and supervisors on implementing and managing contact tracing, addressing challenges, and coordinating efforts. A tabletop exercise to simulate contact tracing activities, identify areas for improvement, and familiarize team leaders with protocols and resources. Training on the CDC's Epi Info VHF database for data managers to track contact tracing activities. Infection prevention and control training for all personnel involved in the EVD response, focusing on proper PPE use. A community engagement module to train all EVD response personnel on the importance of community involvement and effective communication.
